notes: Trade tables and flows are in fine-metal equivalent, an Atlas estimate: the declared value of each flow (CEPII BACI) divided by the year's average price of the metal (World Bank Pink Sheet), never above the customs gross weight. Customs gross weight counts dore, alloys and the base metal they contain, and some declared quantities are wrong; it is given in the note of each row and in brackets after the world exports figure.
The table lists the 13 countries USGS names; its 'Other countries' line (1,000 t, 30% of the total) covers every other producer.
discrepancies: World exports in fine-metal equivalent (Atlas estimate from customs values) 7,080 t (2024) are 2.1x USGS world mine production 3,300 t Au (2025): customs trade can count refined or recycled metal, and metal re-exported from one country to another, more than once, so it is not comparable with mine output (the atlas does not measure how much); USGS is used for production, BACI for trade.

World mine production 2025: the USGS estimate is 3,300 t (rounded); the World Gold Council reports 3,671.6 t (Gold Demand Trends, full year 2025 (supply), https://www.gold.org/goldhub/research/gold-demand-trends/gold-demand-trends-full-year-2025/supply), so the USGS total is 10% lower. The World Gold Council describes its 2025 figure as subject to revision; its own tables are not copied.
